text:
sam_sales: Heads up — POC customer hitting TLS cert errors when their app calls our private endpoint inside their VPC. Works from their bastion but fails from app hosts behind corporate proxy. Error: "certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate"

anna_eng: Can you paste the exact curl/stack trace from the failing host? Also confirm whether they’re using an Interface endpoint (PrivateLink) or just a private hosted zone / route to our IPs.

sam_sales: Quick paste from app host: 
```
curl -v https://private.redwood-internal.example --connect-timeout 5
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to private.redwood-internal.example (10.2.1.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake failed: SSL: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate verify failed
```
They say endpoint is an Interface Endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce). Bastion (same subnet) -> curl works fine. App hosts are forced through corporate HTTP(S) proxy (per their env vars).

jordan_sre: This smells like TLS inspection / corporate MITM. Proxy is resigning TLS with their internal CA so the host fails to verify the chain unless the proxy CA is trusted. Two quick checks: 
1) From failing host run: `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.1.45:443 -servername private.redwood-internal.example -showcerts` 
2) Check `env | egrep -i 'HTTP|NO_PROXY'` and `/etc/resolv.conf` to confirm DNS is resolving the VPC endpoint internally.

max_infra: Also confirm the VPC endpoint security group & endpoint policy. If the app's egress goes out via proxy then the connection never reaches the ENI directly — you'll see the proxy IP as the peer in the tcpdump. If it's reaching the ENI directly you should see the real Redwood IPs.

sam_sales: Ran the openssl on app host, pasted relevant bits: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = CorpProxy CA, CN = CorpProxy Root
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=private.redwood-internal.example
issuer=/CN=CorpProxy CA
---
```
So issuer is the corporate CA, not Redwood's. Traceroute shows next hop is their proxy appliance.

anna_eng: Confirmed — proxy is intercepting. Two remediation paths: 
- Preferred: configure customer's proxy to bypass (no-proxy) for the private endpoint hostname/IP so traffic goes direct to the interface endpoint (no TLS inspection).
- Alternative: add their corporate CA to the app hosts' trust store so the resigning cert is accepted (requires security approval).

jordan_sre: Quick troubleshooting commands to share with them: 
```
# show proxy env
env | egrep -i 'http_proxy|https_proxy|no_proxy'

# test direct TCP to endpoint IP (bypass proxy env)
curl -v --noproxy '*' https://private.redwood-internal.example --connect-timeout 5

# s_client to inspect chain
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.1.45:443 -servername private.redwood-internal.example -showcerts
```
If `--noproxy '*'` succeeds, that proves the proxy is the blocker.

max_infra: If they can’t change proxy policies quickly, a short-term workaround is to route only that endpoint through a NAT that does not use the inspection appliance (eg. place app hosts in a subnet that has direct route to the ENI) or create a policy in the proxy to allow pass-through for `private.redwood-internal.example`. We can also confirm endpoint policy doesn't limit source principals.

sam_sales: Customer tried `curl --noproxy '*'` from app host and it works. They reported app is a containerized service where env vars are injected, so changing NO_PROXY should be straightforward. They want to know the exact host patterns to add to no_proxy and whether there's any TLS fingerprint pinning on our side.

anna_eng: No server-side TLS pinning — platform uses standard TLS certs and will accept normal CA chains. For NO_PROXY add the private hostname and the VPC DNS entry if they use wildcard certs: e.g., `NO_PROXY=private.redwood-internal.example,10.2.1.45` or use CIDR for their VPC range. Also recommend verifying `/etc/hosts` isn't shadowing the name.

jordan_sre: Ask them to also check their container runtime (systemd or k8s) for proxy config; sometimes kubelet or the container runtime injects proxy envs differently. For long term, advise them to route traffic to our endpoint via the VPC endpoint ENI directly so proxies are bypassed.

max_infra: I’ll open a short runbook entry for this case (private endpoint + corporate TLS inspection) with the exact commands and suggested NO_PROXY patterns. Link will be added here in a minute.

deploy-bot: Note: private-endpoint change doc created (#PN-4837) — see https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-endpoint-proxy-inspection

sam_sales: Perfect. I’ll send the runbook to the customer and recommend NO_PROXY change as first try. If they want help changing container env injection I can put them in touch with our solutions engineer. Thanks all.

anna_eng: If they change NO_PROXY and still see intermittent failures, ask for tcpdump (`sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.1.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/pe.pcap`) and we can confirm flow and SNI. If everything points to proxy and they can’t change it, we’ll escalate to eng-private-networking for design help.

sam_sales: Will do. Escalate if needed. :thumbsup:
